content: Hi — I'd like write access to leanprover-community/mathlib4. I'd like to open a PR adding the Jacobian-conjecture counterexample verification to Counterexamples/, hopefully jointly with others. GitHub username: jyh. Many thanks!
Hi, the normal workflow is to create a fork and make a pull request as usual on github, write access is not needed
Welcome! See FC#4474 as formal-conjectures holds conjectures, not Mathlib.
Why are we getting a sudden glut of people asking for access? @Jason Hickey why did you ask for write access? Whatever told you this is several years out of date and it would be nice to fix.

Snir Broshi said:

Welcome! See FC#4474 as formal-conjectures holds conjectures, not Mathlib.

There are other arguments like not wanting to duplicate formal-conjectures, but this particular reasoning doesn't sense to me. There are already proofs in Counterexamples that have "conjecture" in their common name.

Indeed (and I even authored a minor one of those!), but I did not make any general argument or reasoning about this. I merely mentioned that such a PR already exists, and to the repo that holds the Jacobian conjecture, which isn't Mathlib. You could nitpick that I should've included the word "generally" somewhere, sure.
btw FC is relatively new, so the existence of conjectures in Mathlib doesn't necessarily mean they'd be accepted these days (but idk, maybe)
My apologies, I am out of date! I had assumed that I needed permission to submit a PR. OTOH, FC#4474 is a DeepMind repo, should we not submit in parallel to Counterexamples?

My apologies, I am out of date!

Kevin's question is about where this information came from - we want to make sure no one else ends up finding the old instructions.

Hi Eric, I was working from memory from this page, https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/how-to-contribute.html where I thought it said we should ask permission. I should have refreshed myself, it does not say that.

Kevin Buzzard said:

Why are we getting a sudden glut of people asking for access?

I have a feeling this is because of LLM knowledge cutoff dates.
This is Gemini (no excuses, I should have read the guidelines!),
So to be clear, "thought it said we should ask permission" means "Gemini said"?

Thought may be a better term, but I do certainly consult AI, so I'll accept it either way. Please, can you look at this document? https://leanprover-community.github.io/lean3/contribute/index.html#making-a-pull-request-pr

If I read it right, it says we need to ask for permission... 3. Introduce yourself on Zulip and ask for write access to non-master branches of the mathlib repository. Please include your GitHub username in your request. Make your changes on a branch of the main repository.
That's Lean 3, which is clearly marked as obsolete.
@Jason Hickey More directly I'd like to ask: are you using an LLM to write these responses? This is not allowed on this Zulip instance.

This is me, Jason Hickey, a human, flesh and blood. Yes, it has been a while, but you can see my lineage, for example, here: https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/10930755_19 I am/was of the PRL camp, instead of CIC, but mathlib is a huge contribution that we never achieved in PRL. And besides, constructive math is hard. Ping me through email and such if you need confirmation.

That said, I do work with LLMs, so fair enough, I'm sure it will be an ongoing topic of discussion.

Jason Hickey said:

Please, can you look at this document? https://leanprover-community.github.io/lean3/contribute/index.html#making-a-pull-request-pr

Was this document linked from an LLM, or from a wiki page / stackexchange post / etc? If the latter, we should fix the link.

Yes, it is, that link comes from the Gemini query I just posted. I know AIs should not hallucinate, but perhaps if you annotated it right there in lean3/#3 "this is obsolete," it might really convince the LLM that #3 is in fact obsolete...
A robots.txt denying lean3 docs will stop future LLM indexing, although I don't think it will stop user-initiated websearch.

Yes, note that is is coming up as a top result in search (image attached).

If you want faster action:

  1. Request Temporary Removal in Search Engines

If the page contains sensitive information and you need it hidden from Google immediately, you can use Google Search Console. [1, 2]

  • Go to the Google Search Console Removals Tool.
  • Click New Request and enter the full URL of the page you want to hide.
  • Select Temporarily hide page from search results. [1, 2, 3]
  • Note: This acts as a 6-month blackout period. To make it permanent, you must also add the noindex tag or delete the page before the 6 months expire. [1, 2]
That message does not look like it was written by Jason Hickey the human.

Yes, note that is is coming up as a top result in search

For what query?

but perhaps if you annotated it right there in lean3/#3 "this is obsolete,

I can't tell if this is sarcasm; the annotation is right there

Ayiyi, this is not what I am here for, accusations and sarcasm. Look, I want to do some formal math. If you don't like that, just tell me, "We don't like you Jason because you use LLMs in your work." I appreciate the work that you all do, it is far beyond anything I ever did, and it holds a dream that I love. But that doesn't mean I am perfect. I am human, and I make mistakes, and I would ask you to give me just a little bit of leeway. That fact that I can copy/paste does not make me an AI. I thought that takedown info might be helpful, but feel free to use a search engine yourself.

Query: how do I make a pull request to mathlib

(no question mark)

Click on the link. Me, an idiot human, skips directly to the information in question under the heading, "Making a Pull Request (PR)." So I read it -- Me, the idiot human, did not read the banner at the top of the page. How can we train idiot humans to read the whole page and not just the answer to their question? That is actually the real question.

Haha I mean wait a minute , didn’t you just end all of that in a tongue in cheek self-deprecating way, but start it with kind of being offended ?

Seems like you yourself acknowledge it’s a bit of a silly situation though !

Either way , I find it easiest to avoid such LLM accusations if I am simply more succinct and less prose-y.

Not that I’ve ever had such accusations, but to varying degrees a persons style can converge in similarity to an AI, and I advise consciously steering away from that essentially.

Jason Hickey said:

Me, the idiot human, did not read the banner at the top of the page. How can we train idiot humans to read the whole page and not just the answer to their question? That is actually the real question.

We could make it a popup

Fair enough, but you are telling me I sound like an AI, and recommend that I avoid sounding like an AI, as a condition to contribute to this community. For reference to my voice, read this book, and tell me my voice (and my co-authors) . That was guaranteed written before AI, and still passes the AI-duck-test, em-dashes and all. See, "Real World OCaml", https://a.co/d/0aCKBYmx or my sole-author manuscript
https://courses.cms.caltech.edu/cs134/cs134b/book.pdf
maybe a popup is a bit too much in-your-face
but a little better would be to make it not scroll of the top of the screen
like a banner

That fact that I can copy/paste does not make me an AI. I thought that takedown info might be helpful, but feel free to use a search engine yourself.

Apologies for the accusation there; copy-pasting with attribution (be it "the google docs say" or "gemini says") is fine, but we are plagued by new users who are just acting as glue between their chat bot and zulip.

Query: how do I make a pull request to mathlib

Thanks, this is definitely not ideal!

haha Nah bro , I just arrived I never accused you of it.

If i had to make an assessment , I would say I personally think its more likely you ARENT using LLM. Why?
Your use of italics mark up in zulip, typically AI middle manning doesn't bother with it. You use '--' rather than the real em-dash, which AI naturally doesn't do or need to do.

But, your writing style is very very similar unfortunately, so I understand why others said it.

As a thought experiment, I a human, can easily imitate AI and convince others I am an AI, but I am not. Are they silly then? Well not really, cause the appearance is so similar.

I am barely a part of said "community" to talk about "conditions of contribution", but i think broadly in life it is now good to consciously avoid talking like an AI, even if you aren't an AI.
Yes, that's what my wife says, too.

maybe a popup is a bit too much in-your-face

Cookie-gated perhaps, + keeping banner. So on first / irregular visit you get the full pop up.

I can imagine if someone does need to trawl lean3 docs for whatever reason, they may start to go insane if the pop-up keeps appearing.

I suspect that the community will be happy with the counterexample just being in one place.
